trickyParts: The copy test is scoped: it reads only the rich_text object's own display strings and the message's own text with Slack's three entities resolved, and it decides nothing but whether to skip that one object. It never removes a piece already taken and never bears on a piece gathered elsewhere, which is how round 1's containment rule deleted field values.

A Slack client's rich_text copy satisfies the test by construction, since every leaf is a segment of the words the own text holds, once &, < and > are resolved there; a mention, emoji, broadcast or link element carries no display string at all, so it cannot fail the test.
The predicate walks through slackWalkKeys, the same key list the walk itself reads, so the names a display string can sit under stay one list.
An object whose type is rich_text is measured at any depth, so an app's rich_text inside an attachment is read as well.
deviations: The rich_text exception is narrowed: a rich_text object is skipped only when every display string it carries holds no word or is already held by the message's own text, compared after Slack's &, < and > are resolved in that own text; otherwise it is read like any other block. This is the architect's ruling of 2026-10-25T05:18:01Z (Envoy message d7ac4a19e3e6eeb53c232d618d7c8470), which narrows its ruling of 2026-10-25T04:55:00Z (d2bf744d502b32e22f038606045cd18b) and leaves every other part of it standing: exact equality for repeats across all pieces, the one ordered key list per object, the seven display fields, the cut, the deleted-message guard.

RECORDED DEPARTURE FROM THE APPROVED SPEC, named by the architect in the same message: approved spec version 11 says the walk 'never has to know the kind of a block or an attachment' and that 'the one exception is a deleted message'. Both sentences are contradicted by this code, which knows the block kind rich_text by name and has two exceptions. The architect has told the human what the code does and ruled that no new spec version follows.

The order inside one object, the architect's ruling of 2026-10-25T04:55:00Z: an object's keys are ordered once — the display names in rank, then the remaining keys alphabetically — and that order is followed whether a value is taken or descended into.
The exact-equality repeat rule, same ruling: a piece is skipped only when exactly equal to one already taken, the message's own text counted among them, which is what approved spec version 11 states.

Not in this round, all three recorded by the tester as risks and ruled not defects by the architect: a field value exactly equal to one already delivered arrives once, which is what the approved rule says; an attachment's fields arrive after its footer and fallback, which is the key-order ruling; and the reviewer's Security[prompt] shape on fallback and value, which the human has been told about and which stays as approved.
